subject.title: Feature request: support native per-session heartbeat scheduling

question: Should OpenClaw add native persisted per-session heartbeat entries, or should multi-session proactive work stay on cron/plugin-owned scheduling until a narrower core API gap is identified?
rationale: This cannot be resolved as a narrow bug fix because it adds scheduler state, config/API shape, persistence, concurrency policy, and operator control surfaces that overlap existing cron behavior.

options.title: Design native heartbeat entries
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/design tracker for a canonical heartbeat-entry model with storage, migration, scheduling, and observability semantics decided before implementation.

options.title: Defer to cron or plugins
options.body: Close or retitle the request if maintainers decide that explicit-session cron jobs and plugin-owned schedulers are the supported multi-session proactive path.

options.title: Split narrower API gaps
options.body: Extract only concrete missing extension or operator APIs if the native heartbeat-entry product is too broad for core right now.

recommendation.title: Design native heartbeat entries
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/design tracker for a canonical heartbeat-entry model with storage, migration, scheduling, and observability semantics decided before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current heartbeat runner/config blame and recent heartbeat/cron maintenance history make this the best available routing candidate for the product decision.
